questions.question: Choose the correct form of the verb in brackets to complete the sentence: She said that she [finish] her homework before dinner.
Select the correct reported speech form: 'I am sorry,' he said, 'I can't come to the meeting tomorrow.'
options: 'I am sorry,' he said, 'I can't come to the meeting tomorrow.'
'I am sorry,' he said, 'I couldn't come to the meeting tomorrow.'
'I am sorry,' he said, 'I can't come to the meeting tomorrow.' (but note: reported speech changes meaning)
'I am sorry,' he said, 'I won't be able to come to the meeting tomorrow.'
questions.answer: 'I am sorry,' he said, 'I couldn't come to the meeting tomorrow.'

questions.question: Which sentence correctly reports the following direct speech? 'If I had known about the party, I would have gone,' she said.
options: She said that if she had known about the party, she would have gone.
She said that if she had known about the party, she would go.
She said that if she knew about the party, she would have gone.
She said that if she knew about the party, she would go.
questions.answer: She said that if she had known about the party, she would have gone.

Select the appropriate word to complete the idiom: Don't _____ your chances. If you don't try, you might regret it later.
